display.purpose: Masthead name, sheet heads, marquee gothic. Size and wdth chosen per line at runtime to fill the track; starts as an outline and is inked by the brayer.

display-fat.purpose: Case titles, the sliced EXTRA head, the 404 code and pied sorts. Fitted by size alone.

headline.purpose: The centre-column stand head; balanced wrap.

title.purpose: Column heads, contents entries, index sheets, fact boxes.

body.purpose: All running copy; old-style proportional figures; the verse runs at clamp(20px, 1.78vw, 27px)/1.45 justified.

lede.purpose: Sheet ledes, case lines, the EXTRA line.

label.purpose: Links and toggles, dateline, scores; clocks use tabular lining figures.

shadows.name: double-ring
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--ink), inset 0 0 0 4px var(--paper), inset 0 0 0 5px var(--ink)
shadows.purpose: The double-bordered box edge: pill, tab bar, fact boxes, specimen cards, line buttons. A border, not elevation.

shadows.name: plate-ring
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--ink), inset 0 0 0 7px var(--aged), inset 0 0 0 8px var(--ink)
shadows.purpose: Work plate mount, with the 14px chamfer clip.

shadows.name: ink-block
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--ink), inset 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--paper) 60%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Inner hairline on the solid ink button.

shadows.name: loose-sheet
shadows.purpose: Floating paper objects: pill, tab bar, index sheets, fact boxes, stamp (up to 0 14px 26px -14px / 0.55).

shadows.name: held-card
shadows.purpose: Fan cards at rest; lifted 0 34px 50px -24px rgb(20 20 20 / 0.6).

shadows.name: sheet-overlap
shadows.purpose: A case sheet sliding over the previous one.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.value: outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 3px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px var(--alarm)
shadows.purpose: Global focus-visible; the outer ring is paper on the EXTRA sheet.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals: presses, pill slide, feed, cards, notes.

motion.name: ease-io
motion.purpose: Mode swaps: the PRINT/PROOF colour cross-fade (0.8s).

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Pressed state of buttons and the stamp (tab bar 0.96).

motion.name: judder
motion.value: GSAP steps of 45ms, linear, then 80ms power2.out settle
motion.purpose: Every state change lands like a sheet under the platen (language, sound, proof, copy, case entry, intro).

motion.name: slit-feed
motion.purpose: Sheets marked [data-feed] open from a horizontal slit; the EXTRA sheet feeds by the registered --feed number.

motion.name: type-case-tiles
motion.value: grid of ink blocks over red under-plates offset 4px 3px, scaleY in and out
motion.purpose: The language is re-set under the tiles.

motion.name: brayer
motion.value: scroll-driven, pure function of scroll position
motion.purpose: Inks outlined heads; the roller enters left and exits right, never parks.

motion.name: engine
motion.purpose: Drives Lenis (autoRaf off), the WebGL render and all UI; no other requestAnimationFrame loop.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No intro, judder or feed; every head, verse word, cut and rule shows finished.

components.name: Type Case

Box size follows what the web uses most (3x2, 2x1, 1x1); in page order the boxes tile the grid exactly (12 by 6, or 6 by 12 below 1100px). Names in Anybody caps, the big boxes with an italic line on what the language is for. The first time the case is seen, the sorts drop into their boxes.

narrative.overview:
The site is the day's broadside, printed while you watch. Every surface is a sheet of coarse newsprint carrying one black relief ink; each sheet feeds in through a slit, settles under the platen with a small judder, and is replaced by the next. Type is set, not styled: a condensed wood gothic is fitted line by line to the measure on its width axis, a heavy fat-face carries the case titles and the EXTRA, and a nineteenth-century newspaper serif carries everything that is read. Headlines arrive uninked, as outlines, and take ink where a 3D brayer rolls across them with the scroll.

Density is that of a front page: double rules, column rules, datelines, a contents column, captions under every cut. Structure is drawn with rules rather than filled panels. Colour is almost absent by discipline; alarm red is a flood reserved for two places and a marking colour for the press's own marks. Imagery is either a live WebGL relief engraving (tone becomes parallel line, crossed in shadow) or real screenshots of the two live businesses, mounted as plates and shown true-colour only under the loupe.

A second state, PROOF, re-inks the whole sheet as a correction proof: cooler stock, softer ink, red proof-reader's marks and ruled lines, the heads left uninked. It is a cross-fade of registered colour properties, not a separate theme.
keyCharacteristics: One ink on newsprint; red is flood or mark, never decoration.
Display type is fitted to the measure per line, never stretched and never a fixed size.
Rules do the structural work: double rules at sheet heads, single rules between columns, star-capped rules at the ends of a measure.
Boxes are double-bordered with small radii; round shapes belong only to the stamp, the loupe and a key's lettered rings.
Motion is mechanical: judder, slit feed, rolling ink, type-case tiles. One GSAP ticker drives all of it.
Reduced motion shows every finished state at once.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Everything structural is Relief Ink on Newsprint. A second colour never appears as a fill for panels, cards, or buttons outside the EXTRA sheet.

rules.name: The Flood-or-Mark Rule
rules.body: Alarm Red is either a full flood (the engraving band, the EXTRA sheet) or a press mark (focus ring, caret, proof marks, tiles, intro stamp). It is never a tint, a gradient, a hover colour, or a text colour for reading copy.

rules.name: The Registered Colour Rule
rules.body: Theme colours are @property-registered so PRINT and PROOF cross-fade as colours. A new colour role that must follow the mode is registered the same way.

rules.name: The Fitted Line Rule
rules.body: Display type fills its track by choosing size and width per line (Anybody's wdth axis, or size alone for Ultra). It is never scaled with transform, never letter-spaced to fit, and its grid tracks are minmax(0, 1fr) so unfitted text cannot widen the layout before fitting runs.

rules.name: The Uninked Head Rule
rules.body: A display head starts as an outline of the ink colour (1.4px stroke) and fills as the brayer passes, with a speckled mask on the fill. Without motion, or before scripts run, heads show fully inked.

rules.name: The Serif Reads Rule
rules.body: Anything longer than a label is set in Old Standard. Anybody and Ultra are for heads, labels and controls only.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Panel Rule
rules.body: Columns, strips and sections are separated by ink rules (1px between columns, 2px closing a block, a 6px plus 1.5px double rule opening and closing a sheet). Background fills are not used to separate content.

rules.name: The Paper-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: A shadow means a loose sheet. It is always soft, downward, ink-tinted and negatively spread; never offset hard, never coloured, never used on in-page boxes.

rules.name: The Round-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: Only the stamp, the loupe and a key's lettered rings (drawn on the plate, or pinned there as 20px letters on small screens) are round. Everything else is a rectangle with a 4, 6 or 10px corner.

dos: Do separate content with ink rules (1px, 2px, and the 6px plus 1.5px double rule) instead of filled panels.
Do fit display type per line on Anybody's width axis or Ultra's size, and hold it in minmax(0, 1fr) tracks.
Do draw box edges as inset double rings (2px ink, 2px paper, 1px ink) with 6px or 10px corners.
Do keep Alarm Red to its flood (engraving band, EXTRA sheet) and its press marks (focus ring, caret, proof marks, tiles, intro stamp).
Do register any new mode-dependent colour with @property so PRINT and PROOF cross-fade.
Do give every state change the press judder, and let reduced motion show the finished state.
Do keep all motion on the one GSAP ticker; nothing gets its own requestAnimationFrame loop.
donts: Don't use a second hue, gradients, or tinted panels; the world has one ink and one red.
Don't set Alarm Red as the colour of reading-size text on newsprint.
Don't round anything fully except the stamp, the loupe and a key's lettered rings.
Don't set a callout ring on the detail it names, or run its rule through a word: the ring goes beside the detail and the rule through clear space (tools/shoot-work.mjs places them).
Don't give in-page boxes shadows, or give floating sheets a hard offset shadow.
Don't stretch display type with transforms or letter-spacing to fill a measure.
Don't set running copy in Anybody or Ultra.

Don't animate a clip-path with rounded corners, or give an exact circle rings and a soft shadow: Chrome compiles GPU shaders for them the first time they are drawn, mid-scroll. Open by transform, and keep round shapes at 99px on 200px.
